sentences.text: The MGNREGA or Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act is a significant welfare scheme in India.
It was enacted in 2005 to provide legal guarantee for at least 100 days of unskilled wage employment in a financial year to every rural household.
The primary objective is to enhance livelihood security in rural areas.
It aims to create durable assets and improve the rural infrastructure.
The scheme also seeks to empower rural communities by providing them with a source of income.
Eligible beneficiaries include every rural household that applies for work under the scheme.
The application process involves submitting a demand for work to the local Gram Panchayat.
Once the application is received the Gram Panchayat must provide employment within 15 days.
If employment is not provided within this period the applicant is entitled to a daily unemployment allowance.
The implementing authority for MGNREGA is the Ministry of Rural Development at the central level.
State governments are responsible for the execution of the scheme at the state and local levels.
The scheme is funded by the central and state governments in a 75:25 ratio.
Payments to workers are made directly to their bank accounts or post office accounts.
The scheme is reviewed regularly to ensure its effectiveness and to address any issues.
MGNREGA has been a crucial tool in alleviating rural poverty and enhancing livelihood security.
